function.mechanism: Acts as an acidulant that lowers/controls pH and contributes sourness; in leavening systems it serves as an acid component.

adi.basis: No published EFSA E355 re-evaluation opinion/ADI identified in the 18-Feb-2026 official EU state-of-play summary table.

efsa.key_finding: E355 is listed as already permitted before 20 January 2009, but the EFSA re-evaluation entry shows not completed and no opinion publication/link in the latest official summary table retrieved.

fda.notes: Listed in 21 CFR Part 184 (direct food substances affirmed as GRAS); used at GMP with category-specific maximum levels.

adi.basis: Group ADI 0-5 mg/kg bw for adipic acid and selected adipate salts; JECFA 2025 exposure review retained reference to current group ADI and called for toxicology re-evaluation.

concerns.summary: JECFA 2025 exposure scenarios showed frequent exceedances of the current group ADI (0-5 mg/kg bw/day), especially in children/high consumers, with some modeled high-end exceedances in the hundreds to thousands of percent.

Historical toxicology basis includes long-term rat findings of reduced body-weight gain/diarrhoea at high dietary concentrations, indicating dose-related gastrointestinal/systemic effects at sufficiently high intake.

Recent food-contact/packaging studies report adipic-acid-related oligomer migrants with TTC-based concern in some scenarios, but these findings are not direct proof of harm from E355 as intentionally added food additive.

no_concern_confirmed: A 2002 toxicology review reports low acute oral toxicity and no clear genotoxic or developmental toxicity signal in tested systems/species.
No IARC monograph classification entry was identified for adipic acid/CAS 124-04-9 in the currently retrieved classification dataset.

populations: high consumers of foods with higher adipic acid use levels
adi_exceedance.notes: JECFA 2025 reported that conservative exposure estimates often exceeded the current group ADI; e.g., high estimates up to 33 mg/kg bw/day (children) in current-maximum scenarios and up to 410 mg/kg bw/day in current+proposed scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: E355 remains authorized, but the best current quantitative source (JECFA 2025) indicates substantial potential ADI exceedance in high-intake scenarios, especially for children, and recommends updated toxicology/ADI reassessment. No IARC carcinogenic classification or major bans were identified.
key_factors: JECFA group ADI 0-5 mg/kg bw/day with 2025 exposure exceedance concerns
JECFA recommendation to re-evaluate toxicology and reassess ADI
